fields.description:
Provision the per-client bearer PATs the `static` verifier authenticates (ADR
deft-evolutive-mosasaur) and the repo-root local-only client-credential config the epic asks for,
treated like every other box secret: SSM-sourced, materialized on-box, gitignored, never committed.
Single concern: the credential material + its safe delivery — client-side config wiring is olm.

## Approach + rationale (SSM-materialize, NOT rsync — gotcha f600)
The `.env` on the box is rsync-EXCLUDED, so a rotated SSM secret never reaches the box via source
sync. The bearer PATs must therefore be materialized on the box from SSM at deploy time, exactly
like the existing `opcert-guard.map.conf` materialization pattern (a separate SSM-sourced file that
nginx/the app reads), NOT baked into the rsync'd tree. A pure value-rotation (no git change) does
NOT advance `main`, so autodeploy no-ops on it — rotation is operator-driven (re-materialize +
reload), which the runbook must state. Because the `static` verifier loads its token set ONCE at
`__init__` (`StaticBearerVerifier.__init__` → `_load_static_tokens`; no per-request re-read),
"reload" here means RECONSTRUCTING the verifier — i.e. restarting/replacing the `rebar-mcp`
process/container (the ADR 0104 blue-green swap) — NOT merely rewriting the tokens file; an
operator who only re-materializes the file sees NO effect. The runbook states this explicitly.
- Terraform SSM params for the per-client PATs (one per client: copilot/codex/claude) under the
  existing `/rebar/prod/` prefix; `fetch-secrets.sh` wiring to materialize them on the box.
- The `static` verifier's accepted-token set is sourced from those materialized secrets. Transform
  (named so the slice is unambiguous): `fetch-secrets.sh` materializes each per-client PAT from SSM
  into the on-box container env source (`.env`, 0600, rsync-excluded) as
  `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_{COPILOT,CODEX,CLAUDE}`, and emits the tokens JSON the verifier reads
  (`infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json`, `mcp.auth_static_tokens_file`) whose records reference
  those env vars via **`token_env`** — NEVER a plaintext `token` and NEVER the raw PAT inside the
  tokens file (ADR 0050 §4 / ADR 0104: the server holds only SHA-256 digests, supplied via env-var
  NAMES, never literals; `_parse_static_record` rejects a plaintext `token`). The tokens file is
  ALWAYS created even when a slot is blank (bug beb1: a missing bind-mount source becomes a
  directory).
- A **repo-root local-only** client-credential config TEMPLATE (committed) + a real gitignored file
  it renders to, so an operator wiring a client has a documented shape but no secret is ever
  committed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Tier: **real file/CLI + a committed-secret guard test** (test-design §3 CLI + §6 contrast). Oracles:
  - The gitignored real credential path is matched by `.gitignore` and a guard test asserts `git
    check-ignore` returns it AND that no file in the tree contains a real PAT pattern (the negative
    control: the template with a placeholder passes; a planted real-looking secret fails). Proof:
    `pytest tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py -k guard`.
  - `fetch-secrets.sh` materializes the per-client PATs from SSM: the raw value lands ONLY in the
    0600 rsync-excluded env source (`.env` as `MCP_CLIENT_PAT_*`), and the tokens JSON the `static`
    verifier reads (`mcp-static-tokens.json`) references it via `token_env` (never a plaintext
    `token`, never the raw value in the tokens file). Oracle: with a stubbed SSM/aws sink feeding a
    known value → the materialized env source contains the value AND the tokens file loads via the
    real `_load_static_tokens`/`_parse_static_record` path (token_env records); both files are
    gitignored (NOT under the rsync'd tree), and the tokens file is created even when a slot is
    blank (beb1). Proof: `pytest tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py -k materialize`.
  - Config-effect contrast (§6): the `static` verifier (`StaticBearerVerifier` over the materialized
    tokens file with the per-client env var set) accepts a request bearing a materialized PAT and
    rejects an unknown token (401) through the real `_load_static_tokens` read path. Proof:
    `pytest tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py -k verifier`.
- [ ] The runbook documents operator-driven rotation (re-materialize + restart/replace the
  `rebar-mcp` process/container so the verifier re-reads the tokens file; autodeploy no-ops on a
  value-only rotation). Proof: checked via `pytest tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py -k runbook`
  asserting `infra/runbooks/mcp-client-pats.md` documents the re-materialize + reload (restart)
  rotation and that a file-only rewrite has no effect on a running verifier.

## Testing
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py` — the guard, materialization, verifier-contrast,
  and runbook oracles above (RED-first; the ACs are the oracle).
- `make lint && make typecheck` — gate the new Python test module + touched sources.

## Compat / rollback
Additive (new SSM params + materialization). Rollback = remove the params + materialization step;
no existing secret path changes. Never commits a secret (enforced by the guard test above).

Depends on: deft-evolutive-mosasaur (ADR fixes the auth mode = static bearer). Blocks:
unmythical-uninspired-olm (client configs need the PAT values).
